The paper uses an isogeometric boundary element method (IGABEM) based on NURBS to solve electromagnetic scattering problems.
Helmholtz equations are solved using IGABEM for broadband electromagnetic scattering analysis.
Non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS) are used for geometry construction and discretization of integral equations.
A series expansion method is applied to decouple frequency-dependent terms in the boundary element integrand.
Frequency decoupling reduces the computational cost of multi-frequency electromagnetic scattering calculations.
The second-order Arnoldi (SOAR) method is employed for model order reduction of large-scale problems.
SOAR preserves key structural properties of the original second-order dynamical system.
The combined approach accelerates broadband electromagnetic scattering analysis.
Numerical examples validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed algorithms.
The method avoids repeated full integral evaluations at each frequency by frequency decoupling.
The paper cites foundational works on IGABEM, series expansion methods, and SOAR techniques.
